answer: Velocity caps make sybils slow, not just expensive: each identity gets a small quota of rewarded actions per epoch, and every action beyond it demands a verifiable delay puzzle whose difficulty doubles each time. A lone island of honest agents stays under the cap for free, while a farmer herding thousands of clones must solve a dune of rising puzzles, each one burning real time and compute. The zenith of the attack — flooding the economy at scale — collapses because the cost per extra action grows exponentially, so mass fakery becomes a traffic jam of its own making.
